Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA Corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE DILG OPINION NO. J 13 S. 2010 JUN 2 J 200 DIR. HELENA B. HABULAN Executive Director Department of Finance Roxas Boulevard corner Pablo Ocampo, Sr. St. Manila 1004 Dear Exec. Dir. Habulan: This has reference to your earlier letter referring to us the letter of Mayor Virgilio A. Bote, Municipality of General Tinio, Nueva Ecija seeking DOF clearance on that Municipality's proposal to establish stock corporations to be registered under the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). In reply thereto, please be informed that this Department had already answered a related query in DILG Opinion No. 106, series ofL'007. In the said legal opinion, we opined that due to the dual nature and function of a local government unit and from its corporate powers as are granted under the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160), there is no more need for the LGU to create a stock corporation to be registered with the SEC since even without such creation, the LGU already possesses corporate powers as are available to private corporations. Hereto attached is a photocopy of the aforesaid DILG Opinion for your ready perusal. Thank you and warm regards. Copy furnished: Mayor Virgilio A Bote General Tinio, Nueva Ecija Ls/17 Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: . JESU . DO Dire or 111 I

REPUBLIC OF Thill. OIV IIN'U'L'IUOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT Francisco Gold Condonjinium II, EDSÄcor. iVlapagmahal St., Diliman, Quemn Ciiy OFFICE OF 106 21 November 2007 MTV. ROGELIO U. OIC, Law Department City Hall, Makati City Dear Atty. Marasigan: This pertains to your letter requesting legal opinion on certain issues related to the plan of the Sangguniang Panlungsod Of Makati to create a stock corporation to be registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission under the Corporation Code of the Philippines which is to be wholly owned by the City Government of Makati. Said stock corporation is envisioned to become the corporate arm of the city government with respect to its proprietary functions and for other activities to promote the welfare of residents of the City of Makati. In relation thereto, you would now like to be clarified on the following, to wit: I. "Whether or not the City Government of Makati has the authority to create the Corporation [for the purpose of pursuing its proprietary functions, engaging in the delivery of certain basic services or for engaging in projects designed to enhance the economic and social well being of the Makati City residents. 2. Whether or not all the provisions in the attached copies of the Articles of Incorporation and By Laws can be adopted and executed by the officials of the City Government of Makati for purposes of incorporating the Corporation.

3. 4. 5. 6. In -2- Whether or not the DILG has any requirement before the Corporation, or similar entitles, can be treated. Whether or not incumbent elective or appointive officials of the City Government oj the City of Makati can be appointed as incorporators, directors or officers oj the corporation. Whether or not the Corporation, after it is created, can enter into joint ventures, such as the incorporation of subsidiaries with the private sector as joint venture partners, in order to implement projects which are connected with the purposes for which the Corporation will be treated. Whether or not the Corporation can sell its shares to the private sector, or to the residents of Makati City to provide for wider participation in its operations. reply to your first query, a careful reading of the same would give us two impressions: First, that the Sangguniang Panlungsod of the City of Makati will create a stock corporation; or second, the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Makati City will create a stock corporation to be registered with the SEC under the Corporation Code ot the Philippines. If we reply to your query in the light of our first impression, please be informed that under the Constitution, the power to exercise legislative powers is lodged with the legisiauive branch of the government, which is Congress. The Congress, on the other hand, delegated to the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Makati City, through Section IO of RA 7854 (Charter of Makati City), the power of local legislation. The same section further provides for the scope and area of legislation of the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Makati City. At this point, it bears stressing that the Local Governmeot Code applies suppletorily to the Charter of that city. Also, it is not amiss to point out that the power to create government-owned and controlled corporations (GOCC) is an inherent legislative power of Congress. This power, however, was not among the delegated scope of legislative powers of the Sangguniang Paniungsod of Makati, hence, we are of the view that the Sangguniang Panlungsod has no authority to create a local GOCC.

-3- On the other hand, if we are iO reply to your query in the light of our second impression, where a stock corporation is to be created by the city to be registered with the SEC under the Corporation Code of the Philippines, may we respectfully point out the dual nature and function of a local government unit. Under Section 15 oi the Local Government Code, every local government unit created or recognized under the Code is a body politic endowed with powers to be exercised by it in conformity with law. As such, it shall exercise powers as a political subdivision of the national government and as a corporate entity representing the inhabitants of its territory. This is the so-caned governmental and proprietary functions of local government units. in its governmental functions, the local government unit acts as an agent of the State for the government of the territory and the inhabitants. In its proprietary functions, the iocai government unit acts as an agent of the community in the administration oi local affairs. As such, it acts as a separate entity for its own purposes, and not as a subdivision of the State (Lidasan vs. COMELEC, 21 SCRA 496). This dual nature of a local government unit has to be related with the corporate powers of Makati City under Section 3 of its Charter. The same section provides that the city, as a political body corporate, shall have the following pgwers: xxx "(f) to exercise such other powers as are granted to corporation, subject to the limitations provided insthis Act and other laws". it bears emphasizing that by reason of the grant of the power in Section 3 (f) as mentioned, Makati City is endowed with corporate power to exercise the powers as are granted to corporations without need of registering with the Securities and Exchange Commission as required by the Corporation Code. This is because the "corporation" referred to in paragraph (f) abovecited logically pertains to private corporations formed and organized under the Corporation Code. The exercise of such power, however, is made subject to the limitations provided for in the Act itself and other laws. Viewed from the dual nature of the city and from its corporate powers as are granted under the Code, there is no more need for the city to create a stock corporation to be registered with the SEC which is envisioned to be the corporate arm of the city since even without such creation, the city already possesses corporate powers as are available to private corporations.

Parenthetically, although voe cannot find in the Charter of Makati City or in the Local Government Code any jnovision prohibiting the city to create a stock corporation to be registered with the SEC. we believe, however, that the conferment of corporate powers under Section 3 of the City Charter, particularly paragraph (f) thereof, pcoviding for certain qualifications and conditions, will become an effective limitation of the city to pursue its plan of creating the supposed corporation. Having already answered your first query, we deem it not anymore necessary to answer the subsequent queries considering that the same are dependent on an affirmative answer in the first query. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, Affil. MARIUS P. CORPUS Acting Secreta cc: Director Roberto C.
